0x1 - Console display enabled flag value
0x0 - Console display disabled flag value  
0xff - Hardcoded exit code passed to exit function (255 decimal)

0x6FD1DCFC.name: InitializeCriticalSections
0x6FD1DCFC.comment:
Initialize four critical sections for thread synchronization.

Algorithm:
1. Load InitializeCriticalSection function pointer into ESI register for optimization
2. Initialize first critical section (g_pCriticalSection1) by calling InitializeCriticalSection
3. Initialize second critical section (g_pCriticalSection2) by calling InitializeCriticalSection  
4. Initialize third critical section (g_pCriticalSection3) by calling InitializeCriticalSection
5. Initialize fourth critical section (g_pCriticalSection4) by calling InitializeCriticalSection
6. Restore ESI register and return

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
Function uses register optimization by loading InitializeCriticalSection function pointer 
once into ESI and calling through the register four times instead of direct calls.

Global Variables Referenced:
g_pCriticalSection1 (0x6ff3650c) - Points to first critical section structure
g_pCriticalSection2 (0x6ff364fc) - Points to second critical section structure  
g_pCriticalSection3 (0x6ff364ec) - Points to third critical section structure
g_pCriticalSection4 (0x6ff364cc) - Points to fourth critical section structure

Calling Context:
Called during thread local storage initialization as part of multithreading setup.

0x6FD1DD25.name: CleanupCriticalSections
0x6FD1DD25.comment:
Cleanup and destroy all thread synchronization critical sections.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize pointer to start of critical section array (0x6ff364c8)
2. Loop through array of critical section pointers until end (0x6ff36588)
3. For each entry, check if pointer is non-null
4. Skip predefined special critical sections (PTR_DAT_6ff3650c, PTR_DAT_6ff364fc, PTR_DAT_6ff364ec, PTR_DAT_6ff364cc)
5. If not special section, delete critical section and call cleanup function FUN_6ff2cac5
6. Advance to next array entry (increment by 4 bytes)
7. After main loop, explicitly cleanup the four special critical sections
8. Return to caller

Parameters:
None - function operates on global critical section array

Returns:
void - no return value, cleanup function

Special Cases:
- Four special critical sections skipped in main loop but cleaned up explicitly at end
- Array spans 0x320 bytes (200 pointer entries) from 0x6ff364c8 to 0x6ff36588
- DeleteCriticalSection function pointer loaded from [0x6ff330d8]

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6ff364c8 - Start address of critical section pointer array
0x6ff36588 - End address of critical section pointer array  
0x6ff3650c - Special critical section 1 (PTR_DAT_6ff3650c)
0x6ff364fc - Special critical section 2 (PTR_DAT_6ff364fc)
0x6ff364ec - Special critical section 3 (PTR_DAT_6ff364ec)
0x6ff364cc - Special critical section 4 (PTR_DAT_6ff364cc)
0x6ff330d8 - Function pointer to DeleteCriticalSection
0x4 - Pointer size increment for array iteration

Error Handling:
None - assumes all pointers valid, DeleteCriticalSection handles invalid input

0x6FD1DD91.name: AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex
0x6FD1DD91.comment:
Thread-safe lazy initialization and acquisition of critical section by array index

Algorithm:
1. Calculate pointer to critical section slot in global array g_ppCriticalSections
2. Check if critical section at index is already initialized (non-null)
3. If uninitialized, allocate 0x18 bytes for CRITICAL_SECTION structure
4. If allocation fails, call AmsgExit(0x11) to terminate process
5. Acquire global initialization lock via recursive call AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex(0x11)
6. Double-check critical section is still null (race condition protection)
7. If still null, initialize critical section with InitializeCriticalSection
8. Store initialized critical section pointer in global array
9. If another thread initialized it first, free duplicate allocation with DeallocateMemory
10. Release global initialization lock via FUN_6ff2c45f(0x11)
11. Enter the requested critical section with EnterCriticalSection

Parameters:
nCriticalSectionIndex - Index into global critical section array g_ppCriticalSections
IMPLICIT: Uses global initialization lock at index 0x11 for thread-safe lazy initialization

Returns:
void - Function does not return a value, critical section is held upon return

Special Cases:
Lock index 0x11 (17) is reserved for the global initialization synchronization lock
Process terminates with AmsgExit(0x11) if critical section allocation fails
Double-checked locking pattern prevents race conditions during initialization

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x18 (24 decimal) - Size of Windows CRITICAL_SECTION structure in bytes
0x11 (17 decimal) - Reserved index for global initialization lock

0x6FD1DDF2.name: ReleaseCriticalSectionByIndex
0x6FD1DDF2.comment:
Releases a CRT critical section lock by its index.

Classification: Leaf function - wrapper around Win32 LeaveCriticalSection.

Algorithm:
1. Index into g_apCrtLocks array using dwLockIndex
2. Call LeaveCriticalSection on the retrieved CRITICAL_SECTION pointer

Parameters:
  dwLockIndex (uint) - Zero-based index into g_apCrtLocks array

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - No bounds checking on index; caller must ensure valid range
  - Must be paired with prior CRT_EnterCritSectByIndex call

Global Data:
  g_apCrtLocks (0x6fc38644) - Array of LPCRITICAL_SECTION pointers

Called By: 12 functions including CRT_EnterCritSectByIndex, CRT_LeaveCritSectExit

0x6FD1DE07.name: StreamPutChar
0x6FD1DE07.comment:
Writes a single character to a stream with buffering and error handling support.

Algorithm:
1. Validate stream flags - check for invalid flag combinations (0x82 clear OR 0x40 set)
2. Handle buffering reset - if 0x01 flag set, reset position and optionally restore buffer base
3. Setup output mode - clear position, set backup pointer, configure output flags (clear 0x10, set 0x02)
4. Validate special streams - check if stream matches standard descriptors and validate with FUN_6ff3037c
5. Perform stream cleanup - call FUN_6ff30338 if validation passes
6. Choose output path - buffered (flags & 0x108 != 0) or unbuffered output
7. Buffered output - calculate available space, write directly to buffer or call write function
8. Handle buffer exhaustion - get stream descriptor from table and check error flags
9. Error handling - call FUN_6ff30070 if error flag 0x20 is set
10. Unbuffered output - call FUN_6ff30148 with character address and size 1
11. Verify write result - compare returned bytes with expected count
12. Set error state - set flag 0x20 on write failure, return character on success

Parameters:
nCharacter: Character to write (only low 8 bits used)
pStream: Pointer to stream descriptor structure

Returns:
Character value (0x00-0xFF) on successful write
0xFFFFFFFF on error or invalid stream state

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x01: Buffer reset flag
0x02: Output mode flag  
0x10: Buffer restore flag
0x20: Error state flag
0x40: Read-only flag
0x82: Combined invalid flags
0x108: Buffering mode flags
0x24: Stream descriptor stride (36 bytes)
0xFF: Character mask for return value
0xFFFFFFFF: Error return value

Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name    Type      Description
0x00    4     pBase         void*     Base buffer pointer
0x04    4     nPosition     int       Current position offset  
0x08    4     pCurrent      void*     Current buffer pointer
0x0C    4     dwFlags       dword     Primary stream flags
0x10    4     dwFlags2      dword     Stream identifier/handle
0x14    4     reserved      dword     Reserved field
0x18    4     nAvailable    int       Available buffer space
0x1C    4     reserved2     dword     Reserved field  
0x20    4     reserved3     dword     Reserved field

Error Handling:
Invalid flags (0x82 clear OR 0x40 set): Set error flag 0x20 and return 0xFFFFFFFF
Buffer exhaustion with error flag: Call error handler FUN_6ff30070
Write operation failure: Set flag 0x20 and return 0xFFFFFFFF  
Standard stream validation failure: Proceed with cleanup and normal flow

0x6FD1DF1F.name: FormatStringProcessor
0x6FD1DF1F.signature: int FormatStringProcessor(int * pOutputHandler, byte * pbFormatString, uint * ppnArgsPtr)
0x6FD1DF1F.comment:
FormatStringProcessor - processes printf-style format strings with variable arguments

Algorithm:
1. Initialize state variables: dwFlags=0, nStateIndex=0, nCharCount=0
2. Begin character-by-character processing loop of format string
3. For each character, determine processing state using lookup table at 0x6ff333e0
4. Execute state machine transitions based on current state (0-7):
   - State 0: Output literal characters, handle character attributes
   - State 1: Initialize format specifier parsing, reset all flags
   - State 2: Parse format flags: space(0x02), hash(0x80), plus(0x01), minus(0x04), zero(0x08)
   - State 3: Parse field width (decimal digits or asterisk for va_arg)
   - State 4: Encountered decimal point, prepare for precision parsing
   - State 5: Parse precision (decimal digits or asterisk for va_arg)  
   - State 6: Parse length modifiers: I64(0x8000), h(0x20), l(0x10), w(0x800)
   - State 7: Process conversion specifiers and generate output
5. For conversion specifiers: handle integer(d,i,u,o,x,X), float(e,E,f,g,G), character(c,C), string(s,S), pointer(p), written count(n)
6. Apply formatting: field width padding, precision truncation, sign prefixes, case conversion
7. Convert wide characters to multibyte when needed using FUN_6ff30505
8. Output formatted result through pOutputHandler callback
9. Continue until null terminator reached
10. Return total character count

Parameters:
  pOutputHandler (int *) - callback function pointer for character output
  pbFormatString (byte *) - printf-style format string to process
  ppnArgsPtr (uint *) - pointer to variable arguments list array

Returns:
  int - total number of characters processed and output, or negative on error

Special Cases:
  - Field width of -1 indicates unlimited width (0x7fffffff)
  - Precision of -1 disables precision limiting
  - Zero flag (0x08) is ignored when left-align flag (0x04) is set
  - Hash flag (0x80) adds prefixes: "0" for octal, "0x"/"0X" for hex
  - I64 modifier (0x8000) enables 64-bit integer processing

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x6ff333e0 - character classification table for format parsing
  0x6ff33400 - state transition table (8 bytes per character class)  
  0x20/0x78 - valid format character range (space to 'x')
  0x7fffffff - unlimited field width sentinel value
  0x30 - ASCII '0', base for digit conversion
  0x39 - ASCII '9', upper limit for digit checking
  0x2a - ASCII '*', indicates va_arg width/precision
  0x2d - ASCII '-', negative sign character

Error Handling:
  - Invalid format characters fall through to literal output
  - Null string arguments replaced with default "(null)" string
  - Negative field widths converted to left-align with positive width
  - Buffer overflow protection through character count tracking

0x6FD1E660.name: BufferedPutChar
0x6FD1E660.signature: int BufferedPutChar(byte bCharacter, FileBuffer * pBuffer, int * pnCharsWritten)
0x6FD1E660.comment:
Writes a single character to a buffered output stream with automatic flushing.

Algorithm:
1. Decrement the buffer's remaining byte count
2. If buffer has space (count >= 0):
   a. Store character at current buffer position
   b. Increment buffer pointer
   c. Return character value (masked to 8 bits)
3. If buffer is full (count < 0):
   a. Call flush/refill function FUN_6ff2d034
   b. Use its return value as result
4. Check for error condition (-1 return value):
   a. If error: set chars written counter to -1
   b. If success: increment chars written counter

Parameters:
chCharacter (byte) - Character to write to buffer (0-255)
pBuffer (FileBuffer *) - Pointer to buffer structure containing:
  - pbCurrent: Current write position in buffer
  - dwBytesRemaining: Number of bytes left in buffer
pnCharsWritten (int *) - Pointer to character count/status tracker

Returns:
Character value (0-255) on success
-1 (0xFFFFFFFF) on error or buffer flush failure

Special Cases:
If buffer flush operation fails, error state is propagated to caller
Characters are masked to 8 bits (param_1 & 0xff) for return value
Negative buffer count triggers automatic flush/refill operation

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xFFFFFFFF (-1) - Error indicator for failed operations

Structure Layout:
FileBuffer (8 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name         Type    Description
0x00    4     pbCurrent          byte*   Current write position
0x04    4     dwBytesRemaining   uint    Bytes remaining in buffer

0x6FD1E695.name: RepeatCharacterToStream
0x6FD1E695.signature: void RepeatCharacterToStream(uint dwCharacter, int nCount, int * pOutputStream, int * pnErrorStatus)
0x6FD1E695.comment:
Writes a specified character to an output stream a given number of times.

Algorithm:
1. Check if repeat count is positive, return immediately if zero or negative
2. Enter loop to repeat character output nCount times
3. Call FUN_6ff2d88d to write dwCharacter to pOutputStream 
4. Check error status after each write operation
5. If *pnErrorStatus equals -1, terminate early with error
6. Decrement count and continue loop if count > 0
7. Exit when all characters written or error encountered

Parameters:
dwCharacter (uint): Character code to repeat (typically ASCII value 0x20 for space, 0x30 for '0')
nCount (int): Number of times to repeat the character 
pOutputStream (int *): Pointer to output stream buffer structure
pnErrorStatus (int *): Pointer to error status flag, set to -1 on write failure

Returns:
void: No return value, error status communicated through pnErrorStatus

Special Cases:
- If nCount <= 0, function returns immediately without writing
- Loop terminates early if write operation sets *pnErrorStatus to -1
- Used for padding in printf formatting (spaces, zeros)

Error Handling:
- Monitors error status after each character write
- Early termination on first write failure (-1 status)
- Calling function must check pnErrorStatus for final status

0x6FD1E6C6.name: WriteStringToBuffer
0x6FD1E6C6.signature: void WriteStringToBuffer(char * lpszString, int nLength, FileBuffer * pBuffer, int * pnCharsWritten)
0x6FD1E6C6.comment:
Writes a string to a buffered output stream character by character with error checking.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that string length is greater than zero
2. Initialize loop variables and counters  
3. For each character in the string:
   a. Decrement remaining character count
   b. Load current character from string pointer
   c. Advance string pointer to next character
   d. Call BufferedPutChar to write character to buffer
   e. Check if write operation failed (error code -1)
   f. If error occurred, exit immediately
   g. If characters remain, continue to next character
4. Return when all characters processed or error encountered

Parameters:
lpszString (char *): Pointer to null-terminated or fixed-length string to write
nLength (int): Number of characters to write from string
pBuffer (FileBuffer *): Pointer to buffered output stream structure
pnCharsWritten (int *): Pointer to counter tracking total characters written

Returns:
void - No return value; error status communicated through pnCharsWritten pointer

Special Cases:
If nLength <= 0, function returns immediately without processing
If BufferedPutChar fails (sets *pnCharsWritten to -1), loop exits early
String pointer is advanced byte-by-byte regardless of character encoding

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1: Byte increment for string pointer advancement (0x6ff2d90d: INC ESI)
-1 (0xFFFFFFFF): Error status code indicating write failure (0x6ff2d91b: CMP dword ptr [EDI],-0x1)

0x6FD1E6FE.name: ReadAndAdvancePointer
0x6FD1E6FE.comment:
Reads a 32-bit value from current pointer position and advances the pointer by one element.

Algorithm:
1. Read current value from the pointed-to pointer location
2. Advance the pointed-to pointer by 4 bytes (one uint element)
3. Return the value that was at the original position before advancement

Parameters:
ppuCursor - Pointer to pointer tracking current read position in data stream

Returns:
The 32-bit unsigned integer value that was at the current position before advancement

Special Cases:
This function implements a common "read and advance" pattern used in serialization 
and parsing operations. The caller maintains a cursor pointer that gets automatically
advanced after each read operation.

0x6FD1E70B.name: ReadLongLongAndAdvancePointer
0x6FD1E70B.comment:
ReadLongLongAndAdvancePointer - reads 8-byte value from variable arguments pointer and advances pointer

Algorithm:
1. Dereference pointer to get current position in arguments array
2. Advance the pointer by 8 bytes (2 * sizeof(uint)) to skip over the 8-byte value
3. Read and return the 8-byte value from the original position before advancement

Parameters:
  ppnArgsPtr (uint **) - pointer to variable arguments array pointer, modified in place

Returns:
  longlong - 8-byte signed integer value read from the arguments array

Special Cases:
  - Used specifically for I64 length modifier in printf format processing
  - Advances pointer by exactly 8 bytes regardless of actual data alignment
  - Reads value from position before advancement (offset -8 from new position)

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x8 - size in bytes of 64-bit value (2 * sizeof(uint))
  -0x8 - negative offset to read value from position before advancement

0x6FD1E71B.name: ReadShortAndAdvancePointer
0x6FD1E71B.comment:
Reads a 16-bit value from variadic arguments and advances pointer

Algorithm:
1. Advance the arguments pointer by 4 bytes to next argument position
2. Read 16-bit value from previous argument position (offset -4)
3. Combine with high 16 bits of current pointer value
4. Return composite 32-bit value

Parameters:
  ppnArgsPtr (uint **) - pointer to variadic arguments pointer array

Returns:
  uint - composite value with previous 16-bit argument in low bits

Special Cases:
  - Advances pointer before reading value from previous position
  - Combines current high bits with previous low 16 bits using CONCAT22

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x4 - argument stride (4 bytes per 32-bit argument)
  -0x4 - offset to read previous argument position

0x6FD1E729.name: DispatchExceptionHandler
0x6FD1E729.signature: dword DispatchExceptionHandler(PEXCEPTION_RECORD pExcRecord, PVOID pContextRecord, dword dwEstablisherFrame, dword dwDispatcherContext, int * pEAXSaved, int nReturnValue, PVOID pDispatcherContext, char cUnused)
0x6FD1E729.comment:
Exception Handler Dispatcher - Routes C++ exceptions to registered handlers

Algorithm:
1. Validate magic number (0x19930520) in pEAXSaved[0]
   - If invalid, call TerminateException()
2. Check exception flags (ExceptionFlags & 0x66) for early return
   - If flags set, skip to parameter check
3. If pEAXSaved[3] non-zero:
   a. Check if ExceptionCode equals 0xe06d7363 (C++ exception)
   b. Verify magic cookie 0x19930520 in ExceptionInformation[0]
   c. Load handler function pointer from ExceptionInformation[2] + 8
   d. Call handler with full exception context and return result
   e. If handler invalid, call UnhandledException(...)
4. Else if pEAXSaved[1] non-zero AND nReturnValue equals 0:
   - Call TerminateActiveFrame(..., -1)
5. Return success (1)

Parameters:
pExcRecord: PEXCEPTION_RECORD - Exception record from OS
pContextRecord: PVOID - Context record (PCONTEXT)
dwEstablisherFrame: dword - SEH establisher frame pointer
dwDispatcherContext: undefined4 - Dispatcher context value
pEAXSaved: int* - Saved EAX register context (3 int array: [magic, flags, handlers])
nReturnValue: int - Return value from dispatcher (0 = continue)
pDispatcherContext: PVOID - Additional dispatcher context data
cUnused: char - Unused padding parameter

Returns:
dword - 1 if exception handled, implicit from handler if routed

Magic Numbers:
0x19930520 - C++ exception magic cookie (validation marker)
0x66 - Exception flags bitmask for early exit (0x02 | 0x04 | 0x60)
0xe06d7363 - EXCEPTION_CPP_THROW status code (C++ throw)

Related Functions:
- FUN_6fe221a9 - TerminateActiveFrame (frame cleanup)
- FUN_6fe228a9 - TerminateException (fatal handler)
- FUN_6fe21eef - UnhandledException (routing fallback)

0x6FD1E7C4.name: CppExceptionFilter
0x6FD1E7C4.signature: void CppExceptionFilter(PEXCEPTION_RECORD pExceptionRecord, PVOID pContext, DWORD dwDispatcherContext, uint dwExceptionFlag, uint dwRangeTable, char chContinue, int nRangeIndex, PVOID pFrameInfo)
0x6FD1E7C4.comment:
C++ exception filter for structured exception handling and unwind processing

Algorithm:
1. Validate slot address from context against range table bounds
2. Check if exception code is 0xe06d7363 (C++ exception) with 3 parameters
3. If standard C++ exception signature detected, retrieve unwind handler from thread-local data
4. Call exception validation function to verify handler state
5. Search range table for slot address match using SearchRangeTable
6. Iterate through matching range entries comparing slot address against ranges
7. For matching range, iterate through handler count and handler list entries
8. Call handler comparison function for each handler entry to find matching handler
9. If match found, invoke exception handler (FUN_6fb9bc8d) with parameters
10. If no range match or continue flag set, dispatch to alternative handler (FUN_6fb9bad2)

Parameters:
PEXCEPTION_RECORD pExceptionRecord - Exception information (code, parameters)
PVOID pContext - Context structure containing slot address at offset 0x8
DWORD dwDispatcherContext - Dispatcher context value
uint dwExceptionFlag - Exception processing flags
uint dwRangeTable - Pointer to range table for handler lookup
char chContinue - Continue/stop flag (0=stop at first match, nonzero=continue to alternatives)
int nRangeIndex - Exception index for range table search
PVOID pFrameInfo - Frame information structure

Returns:
void (no return value, exception handling state modified via function calls)

Special Cases:
- Slot address -1 is invalid and triggers error
- Slot address >= range table size is invalid
- 0xe06d7363 with different parameter counts handled as non-C++ exception
- ExceptionInformation[2] == 0 indicates special handler case
- Handler count of 0 in range entry skips handler iteration

Magic Numbers:
0xe06d7363 - C++ exception code (VCppException magic signature)
0x19930520 - C++ exception parameter signature validation value
0xffffff00 - Mask for exception flag byte (preserves high 24 bits)
0x10 - Handler entry size (16 bytes per handler block)
0x6c, 0x70 - Offsets into thread-local data for exception handler retrieval

Note: Function uses SSA temporaries optimized away (pDVar1, extraout_var)

0x6FD1E977.name: CppExceptionFilterForUnitActions
0x6FD1E977.signature: int CppExceptionFilterForUnitActions(PEXCEPTION_RECORD pExceptionRecord, PVOID pContext, DWORD dwErrorCode, dword dwDispatcherContext, dword nActionId, int nRangeIndex, int nActionLevel, PVOID pUserData)
0x6FD1E977.comment:
C++ exception filter for unit action execution with range validation.

Algorithm:
1. Get current state data via FUN_6fb9c171()
2. Check if special flag 0x1a is set; if so, execute unit action with SEH
3. If action succeeds (nResult != 0), return early
4. Call SearchRangeTable to get range entry array and bounds (nStartIndex, nEndIndex)
5. Iterate through range entries from nStartIndex to nEndIndex
6. For each entry, check if nRangeIndex falls within [min, max] bounds
7. Calculate entry offset: (field[12] << 4) + field[16]
8. Load pointer at offset-12; if NULL or char[8] is null terminator, proceed
9. Call FUN_6fb9bc8d to process matching range entry
10. Continue to next entry and repeat

Parameters:
- PEXCEPTION_RECORD pExceptionRecord: Exception information record
- PVOID pContext: Context data pointer
- DWORD dwErrorCode: Error code from exception
- dword dwDispatcherContext: Dispatcher state (0x00-0xFF, check against range bounds)
- dword nActionId: Action identifier for validation
- int nRangeIndex: Range index to search within table
- int nActionLevel: Action level/priority value
- PVOID pUserData: User-supplied context pointer

Returns:
- int: 0 if range processing succeeded, 1 if action executed via SEH early exit

Special Cases:
- Magic offset 0x68: State data flag check
- Magic offset 12 and 16: Range entry indices (5-dword entries)
- Magic offset -12 and -16: Pointer and header offsets within entry
- Magic offset 8: Character check for null terminator

Range Table Entry Layout:
  Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  0      | 4    | min        | int  | Minimum range value
  4      | 4    | max        | int  | Maximum range value
  8      | 4    | reserved   | int  | Unused
  12     | 4    | field1     | int  | Multiplier for offset calculation (<<4)
  16     | 4    | field2     | int  | Base offset addend

0x6FD1EA21.name: MatchItemSlotsByIdentityAndFlags
0x6FD1EA21.signature: dword MatchItemSlotsByIdentityAndFlags(byte * pItemSlot1, byte * pItemSlot2, dword * pdwFlagMask)
0x6FD1EA21.comment:
Match item slots by identity and apply flag filters.

Algorithm:
1. Load item name pointer from pItemSlot1[+4]; if NULL or points to empty string, return SUCCESS (1)
2. Compare item pointers: if pItemSlot1[+4] == pItemSlot2[+4], skip string comparison
3. If different pointers, compare item name strings: strcmp(pItemSlot1[+4]+8, pItemSlot2[+4]+8)
4. If string comparison succeeds (iVar1==0), proceed to flag checks
5. Flag filter validation (all must pass):
   - If FLAG_0x02 set in pdwFlagMask: require FLAG_0x08 SET in pItemSlot1, else FAIL (return 0)
   - If FLAG_0x01 set in pdwFlagMask: require FLAG_0x01 SET in pItemSlot1, else FAIL
   - If FLAG_0x02 set in pdwFlagMask: require FLAG_0x02 SET in pItemSlot1, else FAIL
6. If all flags pass, return SUCCESS (1); else return FAIL (0)

Parameters:
pItemSlot1 (byte *) - First item slot pointer with flags at offset 0, item name pointer at offset +4
pItemSlot2 (byte *) - Second item slot pointer with flags at offset 0, item name pointer at offset +4
pdwFlagMask (dword *) - Points to dword with filter flags (0x01, 0x02) indicating which flags to check

Returns:
1 - Items match by identity/name and all enabled flag filters pass
0 - Items do not match or flag filter fails

Special Cases:
- NULL or empty item names (at pItemSlot1[+4]+8) immediately return SUCCESS (1)
- Flag mask 0 (no filters) means all items match once identity passes
- Asymmetric flag checking: filters from pItemSlot1, mask from pdwFlagMask

0x6FD1EA7E.name: ProcessExceptionFrameChain
0x6FD1EA7E.signature: void ProcessExceptionFrameChain(void * pHeadFrame, dword dwFrameFlags, void * pFrameList, int nStopIndex)
0x6FD1EA7E.comment:
Processes exception handler frame chain from current index to stop index.

Algorithm:
1. Save current exception context and establish SEH frame with mode flags
2. Load current frame index from pHeadFrame at offset 0x8
3. Loop while frame index != nStopIndex:
   a. Validate frame index in bounds: 0 <= index < pFrameList.size (at pFrameList + 0x4)
   b. Call exception error handler (FUN_6fb9c2d9) if bounds violated
   c. Load frame handler from pFrameList array at (index * 8 + 4)
   d. If handler present, invoke __CallSettingFrame with code 0x103
   e. Advance frame index: index = pFrameList.array[index * 8]
4. Store final frame index back to pHeadFrame offset 0x8
5. Restore previous exception context
6. Return to caller

Parameters:
pHeadFrame (void *) - Pointer to head of exception frame chain; offset +0x8 contains current frame index to process
dwFrameFlags (dword) - Exception mode/state flags; stored in SEH context at FS:[0]
pFrameList (void *) - Array structure containing frame records; offset +0x4 is max frame count, offset +0x8 points to frame array
nStopIndex (int) - Frame index to stop iteration at; loop terminates when current index equals this value

Returns:
void - None. Updates pHeadFrame->frame_index with final iteration value and restores exception context.

0x6FD1EB32.name: HandleStructuredException
0x6FD1EB32.signature: void HandleStructuredException(PEXCEPTION_RECORD pExcRecord, PVOID pBasePtr, DWORD dwContext, uint dwUnknown, int nFrameCount, byte * pbFrameData, byte * pbRestoreData, int * pnState, int nStateIndex, PVOID pUnwindContext)
0x6FD1EB32.comment:
Handles structured exception by unwinding and restoring execution context.

Algorithm:
1. If restore data provided, copy from frame data to restore buffer
2. If unwind context is null, use base pointer
3. Call exception unwinder with context and record
4. Process frame state with frame count and current state
5. Increment state counter at base offset 8
6. Create SEH context from exception record and parameters
7. If SEH context valid, restore and jump to handler

Parameters:
pExcRecord - Windows exception record structure
pBasePtr - Base address of exception context
dwContext - Exception context flags
dwUnknown - Unknown context parameter
nFrameCount - Number of frames in exception stack
pbFrameData - Pointer to frame data buffer
pbRestoreData - Pointer to restoration buffer (null = skip)
pnState - Pointer to current state value [read/write]
nStateIndex - Current state index in stack
pUnwindContext - Custom unwind context (null = use pBasePtr)

Returns:
void - function always returns (no return value)

0x6FD1EBAD.name: InitializeGameStateFrame
0x6FD1EBAD.signature: dword InitializeGameStateFrame(dword dwFrameId, void * pFrameData, dword dwFrameType, dword dwFlags, void * pContext, int nParam1, int nParam2)
0x6FD1EBAD.comment:
Initialize game state exception handling frame with SEH (Structured Exception Handling) protection.

Algorithm:
1. Save current exception list and link SEH exception frame (ExceptionList = &local_14)

0x6FD1F344.name: ReallocateMemoryWithStrategy

New handler disabled (_NhFlag=0) returns NULL on first allocation failure
New handler enabled retries allocation until handler indicates stop

0x6FD1F79F.name: AllocateMemoryByStrategy
0x6FD1F79F.comment:
Allocate memory using strategy-based allocation system with fallback to heap

Algorithm:
1. Initialize structured exception handling (SEH) with error state 0xFFFFFFFF
2. Check global allocation strategy value (g_dwAllocationStrategy)
3. Strategy 3 (Pool allocation):
   - Verify requested size <= pool limit (g_dwPoolSizeLimit)
   - Acquire critical section lock (index 9)
   - Call pool allocator (FUN_6ff2eb6f) with raw size
   - Release critical section lock
   - Return allocated pointer if successful, otherwise fall to heap
4. Strategy 2 (Block allocation):
   - Calculate aligned size: (size + 15) & 0xFFFFFFF0 (16-byte alignment)
   - Use minimum 16 bytes if size is 0
   - Verify aligned size <= block threshold (g_dwBlockSizeThreshold)
   - Acquire critical section lock (index 9)
   - Call block allocator (FUN_6ff2f612) with size >> 4 (divided by 16)
   - Release critical section lock
   - Return allocated pointer if successful, otherwise fall to heap
5. Fallback allocation:
   - Use minimum 1 byte if size is 0
   - Calculate aligned size: (size + 15) & 0xFFFFFFF0
   - Call HeapAlloc with global heap handle (g_hHeapHandle)
   - Return allocated pointer (or NULL on failure)
6. Restore exception handling and return

Parameters:
dwSize (ulong): Requested allocation size in bytes

Returns:
void *: Pointer to allocated memory block, or NULL if allocation fails

Special Cases:
Zero size allocation converts to minimum allocation (1 byte for heap, 16 for blocks)
All allocations are 16-byte aligned for optimal performance
Critical sections provide thread safety for pool and block strategies

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xFFFFFFFF - SEH error state marker
0x10 (16) - Minimum block size and alignment boundary
0xF (15) - Alignment mask for 16-byte boundary calculation
0xFFFFFFF0 - Alignment mask (inverted 15) for clearing low 4 bits
9 - Critical section index for allocation subsystem

Error Handling:
SEH protects against access violations during allocation
Failed pool/block allocations automatically fall back to heap allocation
NULL return indicates complete allocation failure (out of memory)

State Machine:
State 1: Check strategy 3 → Pool allocation attempt → Success/Fall to heap
State 2: Check strategy 2 → Block allocation attempt → Success/Fall to heap  
State 3: Fallback allocation → HeapAlloc → Return result
State 4: Cleanup SEH and return allocated pointer

0x6FD1F98E.name: CheckFloatingPointModulus
0x6FD1F98E.comment:
Checks if the modulus operation result is less than pi constant

Algorithm:
1. Load dividend value from g_dDividend (0x100282c8)
2. Load divisor value from g_dDivisor (0x100282d0) 
3. Calculate floating point modulus: remainder = dividend - (dividend / divisor) * divisor
4. Compare remainder with g_dPiConstant (pi value)
5. Return 1 if remainder < pi, otherwise return 0

Parameters:
    None

Returns:
    1 (true) if floating point modulus is less than pi constant
    0 (false) if floating point modulus is greater than or equal to pi constant

Special Cases:
    Uses floating point arithmetic for modulus calculation instead of integer operation
    Compares result against mathematical pi constant for threshold decision

Magic Numbers Reference:
    g_dPiConstant @ 0x10027ce8 - Mathematical pi constant (3.14159...)
    g_dDividend @ 0x100282c8 - Global dividend for modulus calculation  
    g_dDivisor @ 0x100282d0 - Global divisor for modulus calculation

Algorithm Step Mapping:
    Step 1-2: FLD instructions at 0x1001ddfd and 0x1001de06
    Step 3: FDIV, FMUL, FSUBR sequence at 0x1001de12-0x1001de18
    Step 4: FCOMP instruction at 0x1001de21
    Step 5: Conditional jump at 0x1001de2a based on comparison flags

Error Handling:

    Relies on FPU flag handling for comparison results

0x6FD1F9F5.name: ProcessLocaleStringTransform
0x6FD1F9F5.comment:
Processes locale-specific string transformation with character skipping and rotation.

Algorithm:
1. Convert first character of input string to lowercase using ConvertCharacterToLowerCase
2. If converted character equals 'e' (0x65), skip to character rotation step  
3. Otherwise, enter character skipping loop
4. Advance string pointer to next character
5. Check locale mode via global DAT_1002e914 (< 2 = table lookup, >= 2 = function call)
6. For table lookup mode: Use PTR_DAT_1002e708 lookup table with character * 2 offset, mask with 0x4
7. For function call mode: Call FUN_1001fbc2 with character value and constant 4
8. Continue until character test returns 0 (non-whitespace character found)
9. Perform character rotation at end of string
10. Save current character and replace with global DAT_1002e918
11. Iterate through remaining string, shifting characters one position
12. Continue until null terminator reached

Parameters:
pLocaleContext - Locale context object containing character mapping data and locale settings
lpszString - Input string to process and transform in-place

Returns:
void - Function modifies string in-place, no return value

Special Cases:
If first character converts to 'e' (0x65), skips whitespace removal entirely
String rotation uses global character value DAT_1002e918 as insertion point
Function handles two different locale modes based on DAT_1002e914 threshold
Character lookup table uses stride of 2 bytes per character entry

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x65 - ASCII 'e', threshold for skipping whitespace removal
0x4 - Bitmask for character classification in lookup table  
0x2 - Stride multiplier for lookup table access (PTR_DAT_1002e708[char * 2])
DAT_1002e914 - Locale mode selector (< 2 = table, >= 2 = function)
DAT_1002e918 - Character value used for string rotation
PTR_DAT_1002e708 - Character classification lookup table pointer

0x6FD1FED7.name: AcquireCriticalSectionForAddress
0x6FD1FED7.comment:

2. If address within range: Calculate indexed critical section
   a. Subtract base address (0x6ff38ba0) to get relative offset
   b. Divide by 32 (SAR 0x5) to get block index
   c. Add offset 0x1c to get critical section index
   d. Call AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex with calculated index
3. If address outside range: Use direct critical section approach
   a. Add 0x20 offset to address for critical section structure
   b. Call EnterCriticalSection with calculated address

Parameters:

Returns:

Special Cases:

- Block size: 32 bytes per indexed critical section
- Direct offset: +0x20 for non-indexed critical sections

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x6ff38ba0 - Start of indexed critical section memory range
0x6ff38e00 - End of indexed critical section memory range (exclusive)
0x5 - Right shift by 5 (divide by 32) for block indexing
0x1c - Base index offset (28) for critical section array
0x20 - Offset to critical section structure for direct addressing

0x6FD1FF06.name: AcquireStructureCriticalSectionByIndex
0x6FD1FF06.comment:

3. If index below threshold: branch to indexed acquisition method
4. If index at/above threshold: use direct critical section method
5. For indexed method: add offset 0x1c (28) to index
6. For indexed method: call AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex with adjusted index
7. For direct method: calculate CRITICAL_SECTION address (pLockContext + 0x20)
8. For direct method: call Windows EnterCriticalSection API
9. Return to caller

Parameters:

- nLockIndex: Zero-based index of critical section to acquire
- pLockContext: Pointer to LockContext structure containing synchronization objects

Returns:

- void (no return value)
- Function modifies global synchronization state

Special Cases:

- Threshold 0x14 (20) determines which acquisition method to use
- Index adjustment +0x1c (28) applied for indexed acquisition only
- Offset +0x20 (32) locates CRITICAL_SECTION within LockContext structure

+0x00   32    data              byte[32]            Reserved data area
+0x20   24    criticalSection   _RTL_CRITICAL_SECTION Windows sync object

- 0x1c (28): Index offset applied before calling AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex  
- 0x20 (32): Byte offset to criticalSection field in LockContext structure

0x6FD1FF7B.name: ProcessEntityIfValid
0x6FD1FF7B.comment:
Validates a stream index and performs stream close operation with critical section protection.

Algorithm:
1. Validate stream index against global stream count limit
2. Calculate bucket index using bit shift (index >> 5) for 32-entry buckets  
3. Calculate offset within bucket using bit mask (index & 0x1f)
4. Access StreamIO descriptor using 2D array indexing with 36-byte stride
5. Check if stream position field has active bit (0x1) set
6. If invalid stream or inactive: set thread error code 9 (invalid parameter)
7. If valid stream: acquire critical section lock for thread safety
8. Call internal close operation (CloseStreamHandle)
9. Release critical section lock
10. Return close operation result or error code 0xffffffff

Parameters:
nStreamIndex (int): Zero-based index into global stream descriptor array

Returns:
Success: Result value from internal close operation (typically 0)
Failure: -1 when stream index invalid or stream inactive  

Special Cases:
Stream index >= g_dwStreamCount triggers bounds check failure
Stream with position field bit 0 clear indicates inactive/closed stream
Thread error code 9 indicates EBADF (bad file descriptor) equivalent

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1f (31): Bit mask for bucket offset calculation (32 entries per bucket)
0x5: Right shift count for bucket index (divide by 32)  
0x1: Active stream bit flag in nPosition field
0x9: Thread error code for invalid parameter (EBADF equivalent)
-1: Error return value indicating operation failure
+0x4: Offset to nPosition field in StreamIO structure

Structure Layout:
StreamIO (36 bytes total):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
+0x0   | 4    | ?         | ?    | Unknown field
+0x4   | 4    | nPosition | int  | Stream position with flag bits (bit 0 = active)

0x6FD1FFD8.name: CloseStreamHandle

Closes a stream handle and cleans up its descriptor entry.

1. Validate stream by calling GetStreamBasePointer to check if stream exists
2. Special handling for console streams (index 1 and 2):
   - Get handles for both stdout (index 1) and stderr (index 2) 
   - Skip handle closure if both point to same underlying handle
3. Get actual stream handle via GetStreamBasePointer
4. Close the Windows handle using CloseHandle
5. Capture any error code from GetLastError if closure fails
6. Clean up stream descriptor by calling CloseStreamByIndex
7. Clear the nPosition field in the StreamIO descriptor array
8. Translate error code if handle closure failed
9. Return success (0) or error (-1)

Parameters:

Returns:

-1 if CloseHandle fails or other error occurs

Special Cases:

double-closure when stdout and stderr point to the same handle.

bucket = dwStreamIndex >> 5 (divide by 32)
slot = dwStreamIndex & 0x1F (modulo 32)

0x5: Right shift count for divide by 32 (bucket calculation)

2. If both flags are set, retrieve buffer pointer from offset 0x8
3. Call DestroyCompressionBuffer to free the allocated buffer
4. Clear compression flag bits by AND'ing with 0xfbf7 mask
5. Zero all structure fields: offset 0x0 (dwState), 0x4 (dwCount), 0x8 (pBuffer)
6. Return with structure in clean state

Returns:

Special Cases:

  If 0x08 flag not set, function returns without cleanup (context not marked for destruction)

Magic Numbers:

  0x08 - Active compression indicator flag
  0xfbf7 - Flag clear mask (clears bits 0x0408 and 0x0800)

Note: Function uses 2 stack-allocated temporaries (uVar1, uVar2) optimized away by compiler

0x6FD20086.name: ValidateAndProcessEntity
0x6FD20086.comment:
Validates game entity and processes resource if flag conditions are met.

Algorithm:
1. Call entity validation function (FUN_6ff31731) with entity pointer
2. If validation fails (returns non-zero), return error code -1
3. Check entity flags byte at offset 0xd for resource processing flag (0x40)
4. If resource flag not set, return success (0)
5. If resource flag is set, call resource processing function (FUN_6ff3193d)
6. Return negated boolean result from resource processing

Parameters:
pEntity (int *) - Pointer to game entity structure being validated/processed

Returns:
-1 - Entity validation failed
 0 - Success (entity valid, no resource processing needed OR processing succeeded)
<0 - Resource processing failed (returns -1 if processing function returns non-zero)

Special Cases:
Flag 0x40 at offset 0xd controls resource processing branch
Resource handle at entity[4] (offset 0x10) passed to processing function

Offset  Size  Field Name           Type    Description
0x00    4     field_0x0           uint    Unknown field
0x04    4     field_0x4           uint    Unknown field  
0x08    4     field_0x8           uint    Unknown field
0x0c    1     field_0xc           byte    Unknown field
0x0d    1     bFlags              byte    Entity flags (bit 0x40 = resource processing)
0x0e    2     field_0xe           ushort  Unknown field
0x10    4     dwResourceHandle    uint    Resource handle for processing

0x6FD200B4.name: FlushOutputBuffer
0x6FD200B4.comment:
Flushes pending write data from output buffer to underlying stream handle

Algorithm:
1. Check if stream is in write mode (flags & 0x3 == 0x2) and buffered output enabled (flags & 0x108)
2. Calculate pending bytes as current_pointer - base_pointer
3. If pending bytes > 0, call WriteToValidatedStream with file handle, base pointer, and byte count
4. If write successful (bytes written equals pending bytes):
   - Clear dirty flag (flags & 0xfffffffd) if buffering flag (0x80) is set
5. If write failed, set error flag (flags | 0x20) and return -1
6. Reset buffer state: set count to 0 and current pointer to base pointer
7. Return 0 on success, -1 on write failure

Parameters:
pFileStream (FILE*): Pointer to FILE structure containing buffer state and flags

Returns:
0 on success (buffer flushed successfully or no pending data)
-1 on write failure (WriteToValidatedStream returned different byte count)

Special Cases:
Stream not in write mode or buffering disabled - no operation performed, returns 0

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x2 - Write mode flag (bits 1-0 = 10 binary)
0x3 - Mode mask for extracting write/read mode bits
0x108 - Buffered output enabled flags (0x100 | 0x8)
0x80 - Buffer dirty flag indicating pending writes
0x20 - Error flag set when write operations fail
0xfffffffd - Mask to clear dirty flag (inverts 0x2)

Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description

0x6FD20119.name: ProcessLockContextEntities
0x6FD20119.comment:
Iterates through lock context table and processes entities based on validation mode

Algorithm:
1. Acquire global critical section (index 2) for thread-safe access
2. Initialize loop counters and result variables to zero
3. Iterate through all entries in global lock context table (g_ppLockContextTable)
4. For each valid lock context entry, check if entity flags contain active bits (0x83)
5. Acquire conditional critical section for the specific lock context
6. Re-verify entity flags after acquiring lock (double-checked locking pattern)
7. Process entity based on mode parameter:
   - Mode 1 (Count Mode): Count successful validations, increment success counter
   - Mode 0 (Fail-Fast Mode): Return error (-1) on first validation failure if bit 0x02 set
8. Release conditional critical section for the lock context
9. Continue to next lock context entry until all processed
10. Release global critical section (index 2)
11. Return appropriate result based on processing mode

Parameters:
nProcessMode (int): Processing mode selector
  - 0 = Fail-fast validation mode (returns -1 on first failure)
  - 1 = Count mode (returns count of successful validations)

Returns:
Mode 0: Returns 0 on success, -1 if any entity with flag 0x02 fails validation
Mode 1: Returns count of successfully validated entities (>= 0)

Special Cases:
- Empty lock context table (g_nLockContextCount <= 0): Returns 0
- NULL lock context entries are skipped silently
- Entities without active flags (0x83) are skipped
- Mode 0 only processes entities with flag 0x02 set

Flag Bits Reference:
0x01 - Entity active/allocated flag
0x02 - Entity requires validation flag (mode 0 processing)
0x80 - Entity processing ready flag
0x83 - Combined active flags mask (0x01 | 0x02 | 0x80)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x83 (131) - Active entity flags mask for initial check
0x02 (2) - Validation required flag for mode 0 processing
2 - Global critical section index for lock context table access
-1 - Validation failure/error return code

Error Handling:
- ValidateAndProcessEntity() returns -1 on validation failure
- Mode 0: First validation failure terminates processing with -1 result
- Mode 1: Validation failures are ignored, only successful validations counted
- Critical sections ensure thread-safe access to shared lock context table

Structure Layout:
LockContext structure (accessed at offset 0x0C for flags):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | ?    | data       | ?    | Context data array
0x0C   | 4    | flags      | uint | Entity status and control flags

0x6FD201BD.name: StreamOperationWrapper
0x6FD201BD.signature: uint StreamOperationWrapper(uint dwStreamIndex, int nParam2, uint dwParam3)
0x6FD201BD.comment:
Thread-safe wrapper for stream operations that validates stream index and provides exclusive access.

2. Calculate bucket index (dwStreamIndex >> 5) and within-bucket index (dwStreamIndex & 0x1f)

0x1f (31): Mask for within-bucket index (modulo 32)

0x6FD20222.name: WriteFileData
0x6FD20222.signature: int WriteFileData(DWORD nStreamHandle, char * lpszData, DWORD dwDataSize)
0x6FD20222.comment:
Writes data to a stream with automatic text mode line ending conversion (LF to CRLF).

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameters - return 0 if dwDataSize is zero
2. Calculate stream descriptor array index (nStreamHandle >> 5) and slot (nStreamHandle & 0x1F)  
3. Check append mode flag (0x20) - seek to end if set
4. Branch based on text/binary mode flag (0x80):
   a. Binary mode: Write data directly using WriteFile API
   b. Text mode: Process character-by-character with LF to CRLF conversion
5. Text mode processing loop:
   a. Copy characters to 1K buffer, inserting CR before each LF
   b. Track newlines added for accurate byte count calculation
   c. Write buffer when full (1024 bytes) or all input processed
   d. Continue until all input data processed
6. Handle WriteFile errors by calling GetLastError and TranslateErrorCode
7. Check EOF marker detection flag (0x40) - return 0 if first byte is 0x1A
8. Set thread context error codes for specific error conditions
9. Return total bytes written minus newlines added, or -1 on error

Parameters:
nStreamHandle - Stream handle containing descriptor index in upper 27 bits and slot in lower 5 bits  
lpszData - Pointer to data buffer to write
dwDataSize - Number of bytes to write from data buffer

Returns:
Success: Number of bytes from original buffer written (excluding added CR characters)
Error: -1 indicating write failure or stream error
Zero: If dwDataSize is 0 or EOF marker (0x1A) detected in text mode

Special Cases:
EOF marker (0x1A) detection causes immediate return of 0 in text mode
Error code 5 (access denied) triggers special thread context field handling
Buffer size limited to 1024 bytes for text conversion requiring chunked writes

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x20 (32) - Append mode flag in stream position field
0x40 (64) - EOF detection flag in stream position field  
0x80 (128) - Text mode flag in stream position field
0x1A (26) - EOF marker character (Ctrl+Z)
0x400 (1024) - Text conversion buffer size
0x1F (31) - Bit mask for slot index extraction
0x5 (5) - Access denied error code
0x9 (9) - Thread context error field value for access denied
0x1C (28) - Thread context error field value for EOF marker

Error Handling:
WriteFile failure triggers GetLastError and TranslateErrorCode calls
Access denied (error 5) sets thread context fields to specific values
All other errors call TranslateErrorCode for error mapping
EOF marker detection in text mode with flag 0x40 returns success

Structure Layout:
StreamIO structure (36 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type    | Description
0x00   | 4    | pBase      | HANDLE  | File handle for WriteFile calls  
0x04   | 4    | nPosition  | uint    | Position flags (0x20=append, 0x40=EOF detect, 0x80=text mode)
[Additional fields at higher offsets not accessed by this function]

0x6FD203B0.name: MemoryMoveOverlapSafe
0x6FD203B0.signature: void * MemoryMoveOverlapSafe(void * pDestination, void * pSource, uint dwByteCount)
0x6FD203B0.comment:
Optimized memory move implementation with overlap detection and alignment optimization.

Algorithm:
1. Check for overlapping memory regions (source and destination ranges overlap)
2. If overlapping regions detected, copy backwards from end to start to avoid corruption
3. If no overlap, copy forwards from start to end for better cache performance
4. For both directions, optimize copying using 4-byte aligned transfers when possible
5. Handle misaligned data by copying individual bytes first to reach alignment
6. Perform bulk 4-byte transfers in optimized loop (unroll threshold of 8 iterations)
7. Copy remaining bytes (0-3) using individual byte transfers

Parameters:
pDestination - Destination memory buffer to copy data to
pSource - Source memory buffer to copy data from  
dwByteCount - Number of bytes to copy between buffers

Returns:
void * - Returns original destination pointer (pDestination) for function chaining

Special Cases:
Zero byte count - Returns immediately without any memory operations
Misaligned pointers - Falls back to byte-by-byte copying with alignment handling
Large transfers - Uses optimized 4-byte transfers with loop unrolling for performance

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x4 (4) - Alignment boundary and 4-byte transfer size
0x3 (3) - Alignment mask to check 4-byte boundary alignment  
0x7 (7) - Loop unrolling threshold for optimized bulk transfer

Error Handling:
No explicit error checking - assumes valid memory regions and non-null pointers
Overlap detection prevents memory corruption during overlapping copies
Alignment optimization ensures optimal performance on x86 architecture

0x6FD206E5.name: ParseModeAndOpenFile
0x6FD206E5.signature: FILE * ParseModeAndOpenFile(LPCSTR lpszFilePath, char * szMode, uint dwPermissions, FILE * pFileHandle)
0x6FD206E5.comment:
Parses fopen() style mode string and opens a file with specified permissions.

Algorithm:
1. Read first character of mode string to determine base access mode
2. Set dwOpenFlags based on 'r' (read), 'w' (write/create), 'a' (append)
3. Set dwFileFlags with read/write bits from g_dwDefaultFileFlags
4. Parse additional mode characters in loop:
   - '+' enables read+write mode (0x80 flag)
   - 'b' sets binary mode (0x8000)
   - 't' sets text mode (0x4000)
   - 'T' sets temporary file (0x1000)
   - 'D' sets delete-on-close (0x40)
   - 'R' sets random access hint (0x10)
   - 'S' sets sequential access hint (0x20)
   - 'c' enables commit mode (0x4000 in flags)
   - 'n' disables commit mode
5. Call internal open function with parsed flags
6. If successful, initialize FILE structure fields and increment open file count
7. Return pointer to FILE structure or NULL on failure

Parameters:
- lpszFilePath (LPCSTR): Path to the file to open
- szMode (char*): fopen-style mode string (r/w/a with optional b/t/+/etc)
- dwPermissions (uint): File permission flags for creation
- pFileHandle (FILE*): Pre-allocated FILE structure to populate

Returns:
- FILE* pointer to populated structure on success
- NULL (0x0) on invalid mode or open failure

Magic Numbers:
- 0x109: Append mode flags (O_CREAT | O_APPEND)
- 0x301: Write mode flags (O_CREAT | O_TRUNC | O_WRONLY)
- 0x1a4: Default file permissions (octal 0644)

0x6FD20855.name: AllocateStreamStructure
0x6FD20855.comment:
Allocate and initialize a new stream structure slot from the global stream table.

Algorithm:
1. Acquire critical section lock (index 2) for global stream table access
2. Iterate through all stream structure slots (0 to g_dwStreamStructureCount-1)
3. For each slot:
   a. Load pointer from g_pStreamStructureTable[nSlotIndex]
   b. If pointer is NULL (empty slot found):
      - Allocate 0x38 bytes of memory for new stream structure
      - Store pointer in table
      - If allocation successful:
        * Initialize critical section at offset +0x20 within structure
        * Enter critical section
        * Zero-initialize structure fields (offsets 0, 4, 8, 12, 28)
        * Set field at offset 16 (0x10) to 0xffffffff
      - Break from loop
   c. If pointer non-NULL, check OwningThread field (offset 0xc) bits [1:0] and [7:7]:
      - If flags clear (flags & 0x83 == 0):
        * Acquire critical section on existing slot
        * Re-check flags after acquisition
        * If still clear, zero-initialize structure fields (goto LAB_6fb9f238)
        * Release critical section on failure/mismatch
      - If flags set, continue to next slot
4. Release critical section lock (index 2)
5. Return pointer to allocated/initialized stream structure or NULL

Parameters:
  None

Returns:
  Pointer to allocated and initialized stream structure (void *), or NULL if all slots occupied/allocation failed

Special Cases:
  - Magic size 0x38 bytes for stream structure allocation
  - Critical section at offset +0x20 within structure
  - Field at offset +0x10 initialized to 0xffffffff (possibly busy/invalid flag)
  - Reuses existing allocated slots if critical section not held
  - Loops exit early on successful allocation or slot found

Structure Layout (Stream Structure, 0x38 bytes):
  Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
  0x00   | 4    | dwFieldZero | uint | Always initialized to 0
  0x04   | 4    | dwFieldFour | uint | Always initialized to 0
  0x08   | 4    | dwFieldEight | uint | Always initialized to 0
  0x0c   | 1    | bFlags | byte | Flags (bits 0, 1, 7 significant)
  0x10   | 4    | dwFieldSixteen | uint | Initialized to 0xffffffff (busy marker)
  0x1c   | 4    | dwFieldTwentyEight | uint | Always initialized to 0
  0x20+  | ~    | CriticalSection | CRITICAL_SECTION | Windows critical section structure

0x6FD2091D.name: ConvertCharacterToLowerCase
0x6FD2091D.comment:
Convert ASCII uppercase character to lowercase with locale support.

Algorithm:
1. Check if locale functionality is available via g_dwLocaleAvailableFlag
2. If locale not available, perform simple ASCII conversion:
   - Validate character is in range 0x41-0x5A (A-Z)
   - Add 0x20 to convert to lowercase (a-z)
3. If locale is available, use critical section protection:
   - Increment g_dwCriticalSectionCounter using InterlockedIncrement
   - Check if critical section limit exceeded (g_dwCriticalSectionLimit != 0)
   - If limit exceeded, enter critical section via FUN_6ff2c3fe(0x13)
   - Call locale-aware conversion function FUN_6ff2bdda with context and character
   - Exit critical section appropriately based on lock state
4. Return converted character or original if no conversion needed

Parameters:
dwCharacter (uint): ASCII character code to convert to lowercase (0-255)

Returns:
uint: Converted lowercase character code, or original character if:
  - Character is not uppercase letter (outside A-Z range)
  - Locale conversion fails or is unavailable

Special Cases:
- Non-ASCII characters (> 127) depend on locale implementation
- Critical section timeout handled by limit check mechanism
- Function maintains thread safety through InterlockedIncrement/Decrement

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x40 (64): ASCII '@', one less than 'A' for range check
0x5A (90): ASCII 'Z', upper bound for uppercase letters  
0x5B (91): ASCII '[', one more than 'Z' for range check
0x20 (32): Offset between uppercase and lowercase ASCII (A=65, a=97)
0x13 (19): Critical section ID for locale operations

Error Handling:
- Invalid character range: Returns original character unchanged
- Critical section failure: Handled by Windows synchronization primitives
- Locale function failure: Returns result from FUN_6ff2bdda (may be original)

0x6FD20A57.name: ReadByteFromBufferStream
0x6FD20A57.comment:
Read next byte from stream buffer, handling validation and property checks.

Algorithm:
1. Load stream flags from pStreamBuffer[3] (offset 0xC)
2. Check if stream is active (flags & 0x83 != 0) and not in closed state (flags & 0x40 == 0)
3. If not yet read-enabled (flags & 0x2 == 0):
   a. Set read-enabled flag (0x1) on stream state
   b. If stream not blocked (flags & 0x10C == 0), call FUN_6fba1db1 to initialize
   c. Else copy buffer pointer from pStreamBuffer[2] to pStreamBuffer[0]
4. Call ValidateAndProcessEntitySlot to validate buffer position and get remaining count
5. Store result count in pStreamBuffer[1]
6. If result valid (non-zero, not -1):
   a. Check if stream property has flags 0x82 set, if so set property flag 0x2000
   b. If buffer at position 0x200 and flags have 0x8 but not 0x400, update to 0x1000
   c. Decrement result count and store back to pStreamBuffer[1]
   d. Load byte from buffer pointer at pStreamBuffer[0], increment pointer
   e. Return the byte value
7. Else (error case):
   a. Set error flags based on return value (0x10 or 0x20)
   b. Zero out pStreamBuffer[1] count
8. Return 0xFFFFFFFF if stream validation failed

Parameters:
pStreamBuffer (uint *): Pointer to stream control structure with fields at offsets 0-6:
  [0] = data buffer pointer (byte *)
  [1] = remaining count / result code (uint)
  [2] = buffer start position (byte *)
  [3] = stream flags (uint): bits 0x1=read-enabled, 0x2=read-pending, 0x8=position-check, 0x40=closed, 0x400=partial, 0x10C=blocked
  [4] = stream property ID (uint, 0xFFFFFFFF for default)
  [5] = reserved/internal
  [6] = buffer position code (uint: 0x200 or 0x1000)

Returns:
uint: Next byte from stream (0x00-0xFF), or 0xFFFFFFFF if stream error/closed

Special Cases:
- Returns 0xFFFFFFFF if stream already closed (flags & 0x40) or validation failed
- Returns 0xFFFFFFFF if property validation failed (FUN_6fba1db1 or result code -1)
- Magic number 0x82: Property validation mask for state bits 1 and 7
- Magic number 0x2000: Property indicator flag set on successful validation
- Magic number 0x24: Property table entry stride (36 bytes per entry)
- Magic number 0x1f: Property index bitmask (32 entries per table array slot)

0x6FD20B98.name: ProcessStreamDataWithLineEnding
0x6FD20B98.signature: int ProcessStreamDataWithLineEnding(uint dwFileIndex, char * lpszBuffer, uint dwMaxBytes)
0x6FD20B98.comment:
Reads from file handle with text-mode line ending conversion.

Converts Windows CR/LF line endings to Unix LF and detects Ctrl-Z EOF.

Algorithm:
1. Validate buffer pointer not NULL, check file handle entry flags
2. If buffered mode (0x48) and pending lookahead char present, prepend it
3. Call Windows ReadFile API to read raw bytes into buffer
4. On error: map errno 5 to EBADF(9) and return -1; for 0x6d return 0
5. If text mode (0x80 flag) is set, process line ending conversion:
   a. Skip CR if followed by LF (convert CR/LF to LF)
   b. Handle Ctrl-Z (0x1A) as EOF marker with flag 0x40 check
   c. For edge cases at buffer boundary, read one lookahead byte

Parameters:
- dwFileIndex (uint): File handle index into g_ppFileHandleTable array
- lpszBuffer (char*): Destination buffer for read data output
- dwMaxBytes (uint): Maximum bytes to read into buffer

Returns:
- Bytes read on success (may be less than dwMaxBytes)
- 0 on EOF or null buffer or ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE
- -1 on read error with errno set

- 0x80: Text mode flag (convert CR/LF to LF)
- 0x1A (26): Ctrl-Z EOF marker character
- 0x6D (109): ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE Windows error code

0x6FD20D71.name: ConvertDateTimeToTimestamp
0x6FD20D71.signature: int ConvertDateTimeToTimestamp(int nYear, int nMonth, int nDay, int nHour, int nMinute, int nSecond, int nDaylightSavingFlag)
0x6FD20D71.comment:
Converts date and time components to a Unix-style timestamp value.

Algorithm:
1. Validate year is in supported range (1900-1994, offset from 0x76c base)
2. Return -1 if year is outside valid range [0x46, 0x8a] from base
3. Calculate cumulative days from month table at g_adDaysInMonths[nMonth]
4. Add specified day to cumulative month days
5. Apply leap year adjustment: if year divisible by 4 and month > 2, add 1 day
6. Call FUN_6ff306b5() to update internal state
7. Calculate total timestamp: ((nHour + (yearOffset * 365 + daysFromMonth + (year-1)/4) * 24) * 60 + nMinute) * 60 + baseOffset + second
8. Apply timezone adjustment if nDaylightSavingFlag == 1 or timezone check passes
9. Return final timestamp value

Parameters:
nYear - Year value (1900-1994 supported range)
nMonth - Month index (0-11, used to index days table)
nDay - Day of month (1-31)
nHour - Hour component (0-23)
nMinute - Minute component (0-59) 
nSecond - Second component (0-59)
nDaylightSavingFlag - DST flag: 1=apply DST, -1=check timezone, 0=standard time

Returns:
Calculated timestamp as signed integer
-1 if year is outside supported range

Special Cases:
Leap year handling: Years divisible by 4 get +1 day if month > February
Timezone adjustment: Applied based on g_dwTimezoneFlag and DST settings
Base offset: 0x7c558180 provides epoch adjustment

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x76c (1900) - Base year offset for calculations
0x46 (70) - Minimum year offset (1970)
0x8a (138) - Maximum year offset (2038)
0x16d (365) - Days per year for calculation
0x18 (24) - Hours per day
0x3c (60) - Minutes per hour, seconds per minute
0x7c558180 - Unix epoch base offset
